comment: Hand-picked inputs to build.py. Everything else in wiki-data.js comes from the ZIM.
topics_comment: The pool: game content by topic (keys as in index.html's TOPICS), an article going to the first topic whose categories it is in. Rolls draw a topic, then an article, and never take the start and target from the same topic. Not Weapons: on the wiki that holds only weapons from Minecraft: The Manga, while the game's weapons are in Items. Not Gameplay, which is the mechanics family.
not_content_comment: Pages in game categories that aren't game content: other editions, list and set index pages. Only Chaos rolls them. The titles are list pages no category marks.
shares_comment: Popular is this share of the pool, best linked from outside navboxes. Deep cuts is this share of each topic, least linked among the articles linked well enough to be a target. See RESEARCH.md.
families_comment: Content the player can add with the Content checkboxes (keys as in index.html's FAMILIES), by category. Articles in them are left out of the pool otherwise. Education is its four exact categories: the broad Minecraft Education category also holds Brewing, Charcoal and Dye.
spinoffs_comment: Namespaces of other games, each a Spin-offs checkbox: its pages can be rolled and links into it go live.
research_comment: Only report.py reads this: the Popular and Deep cuts shares its Pool designs section compares, besides the ones in use, and the sweet spot's range of good first clicks. See RESEARCH.md.
hubs_comment: No hubs rule: links to these and their redirects are dead. Picked from the pages with the most incoming and outgoing links (report.py lists candidates), leaving out specific content (Diamond, Chest, Water…) that makes a fair target.
namespaces_comment: The ZIM holds articles and categories plus the wiki's own content namespaces (Tutorial, Dungeons…), and build.py adds those and their talk namespaces. Links into these other namespaces still appear on live pages, so they are listed by hand (from meta=siteinfo).
